content: Certain drugs and their interactions require careful consideration to avoid adverse effects or reduced efficacy. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions and recommendations for their management: 1. Talazoparib and BCRP Inhibitors: If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor the patient closely for potential adverse reactions. 2. Tazemetostat and Velpatasvir/Voxilaprevir: Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 3. Tecovirimat and Velpatasvir/Voxilaprevir: Tecovirimat, a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19, increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Additionally, tecovirimat decreases their levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Tepotinib and Velpatasvir/Voxilaprevir: Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of the P-gp substrate as per its product labeling. 5. Tipranavir and Velpatasvir: Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Trofinetide and Voxilaprevir: Trofinetide, an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may increase plasma levels of substrates for these transporters, including voxilaprevir. Avoid co-administration with sensitive substrates. 7. Tucatinib and Velpatasvir/Voxilaprevir: Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as per product labeling. 8. Vadadustat and Velpatasvir: Monitor for adverse effects and adjust the substrate dose as needed. 9. Voclosporin and Voxilaprevir: Voclosporin, an OATP1B1 inhibitor, may increase the concentration of OATP1B1 substrates like voxilaprevir. Monitor for adverse reactions when co-administered. 10. Voriconazole and Velpatasvir: Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Voxilaprevir and Zavegepant (Intranasal): Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 12. Rifampin and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir/Voxilaprevir: Rifampin significantly decreases the serum concentrations of sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir. Avoid co-administration. 13. Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Reactivation: Reactivation of HBV has been reported in patients treated with sofosbuvir-containing regimens. Monitor for HBV reactivation and manage accordingly. 14. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding Considerations: There is no adequate human data to determine the risk of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir on pregnancy outcomes. It is also unknown if these drugs are distributed in human breast milk. Consider the benefits of breastfeeding alongside the mother’s clinical need for the drug and potential adverse effects on the infant. 15. Mechanism of Action: Sofosbuvir: Inhibits HCV NS5B RNA-dependent polymerase, suppressing viral replication. Velpatasvir: A pangenotypic HCV NS5A inhibitor essential for viral replication. Voxilaprevir: A pangenotypic NS3/4A protease inhibitor required for proteolytic cleavage of the HCV-encoded polyprotein into mature forms. 16. Storage and Administration: These drugs should be taken with food, stored below 30°C (86°F), and dispensed only in their original container. 17. Adverse Effects: Common: Headache (21-23%), fatigue (17-19%), diarrhea (13-14%), nausea (10-13%), asthenia (4-6%), and insomnia (3-6%). Serious: Symptomatic bradycardia has been reported in patients taking amiodarone with sofosbuvir-containing regimens. Skin reactions, including rashes with blistering or angioedema-like swelling, have also been observed. This information is intended for educational purposes and should be used in conjunction with clinical judgment and current product labeling. Always consult the applicable plan provider for the most up-to-date formulary information.
